added_provisions.reason: The Q01 conclusion (CL-M112-Q01-010) and its application step (CL-M112-Q01-007) assert that the parties and the two witnesses must execute the deed before Lal Peiris, but no provision in the map said so: rule (22) fixes the area and the language of attestation and rule (16)(a) the description of the land. Section 31 rule (12) supplies the missing requirement that the executant and the witnesses sign in the notary's presence and in one another's presence, and it is what connects the place of signing to the area restriction in rule (22). Added as a supporting provision of Q01 and cited by those two claims.

The Q02 answer turns on rule (29) as it stood in April 2018, and the corpus consolidation of section 31 carries the post-2024 text. Notaries (Amendment) Law No. 20 of 1976 s.10(1), which is in the corpus, substituted rule (29) and sets the whole rule out, so the April 2018 wording is available from corpus text instead of being inferred from the amendment log. It also confirms that the accompanying list was then in the Form F, the Form F 1 being the 6-2024 s.3(9) substitution. Added as a supporting provision of Q02 and cited by CL-M112-Q02-002.

question_decisions.note: The answer follows from statute. All three indispensable provisions (rule (22), section 4A, rule (13)) are verified and are the April 2018 text. Rule (12) added as a supporting provision to carry the execution-in-his-presence requirement the conclusion relies on; hop count left at 2, because rule (12) is a further first-order rule on the same facts and not another link in the rule (22) chain. CL-M112-Q01-001 marked disputed: the notarial-attestation requirement it states sits in the part of Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 that the corpus holds only in its post-2022 form.

Both indispensable provisions verified, and the rule (26) numbering doubt raised by the researcher is resolved from the corpus by 47-2011 s.3. 20-1976 s.10 added so the April 2018 text of rule (29) rests on corpus text. The 15 April 2018 deadline follows from the words of both rules. The two claims that rest on section 34 (CL-M112-Q02-005, CL-M112-Q02-010) are marked disputed: the corpus holds only the 2022 substitution, so that a rule (29) breach was an offence in April 2018 cannot be shown from the corpus. Neither claim is load-bearing for the duty itself, so the question stays proposed_gold.

Block confirmed. 43-1982 s.2 charges duty "at the prescribed rate" and s.69 leaves rates to regulations; 12-2006 s.3 leaves rates to a Ministerial Order. Searching the corpus for a rate turns up nothing on point - the only "per centum" figures in the Stamp Duty Act are the s.45 default penalty and the s.54 spoiled-stamp deduction - and 6-1990 s.37, the only provincial charging section held, reaches only property situated in the Western Province. The base and the payer are established; the money figure is not derivable.

Block confirmed on the corpus as it stands, but recorded as a disagreement for the lawyer. 12-2006 s.9 gives two limbs and resolves them "as the case may be" by reference to List I of the Ninth Schedule, which is not in the corpus, and no Southern Province finance statute is held. edges 12-2006/s9 returns no incoming or outgoing edges, so the corpus offers no route to the selecting provision. A lawyer may well hold that the property-situated limb governs a land transfer and that the answer is the Southern Provincial Council, in which case the question becomes answerable and only the receiving office remains open.

disagreements.researcher_position: Q04 cannot be answered because s.9 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act leaves the choice between the place of execution and the place where the property is situated to List I of the Ninth Schedule, which is not in the corpus.
disagreements.verifier_position: The block is right on corpus text alone, but the choice may be settled outside the corpus: stamp duty on a transfer of immovable property is a devolved provincial levy tied to the situation of the land, which would select the Southern Provincial Council for a Matara land executed in Colombo. The corpus cannot decide this; a lawyer can.

disagreements.researcher_position: Rule (6) of section 31 was not among the rules substituted by Act No. 47 of 2011, Act No. 31 of 2022 or Act No. 6 of 2024, so the quoted text stood in April 2018.
disagreements.verifier_position: Rule (6) was substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(4). The substituted text is word for word what is quoted, so the quotation is almost certainly also the pre-2022 wording, but the corpus does not hold the pre-2022 text and cannot confirm it. The provision is supporting only, so this does not block any question.

unsupported_claims: CL-M112-Q01-010 and CL-M112-Q01-007 asserted that the parties and the two witnesses must execute the deed before the notary, a requirement stated by no provision then in the map. Fixed by adding PROV-M112-901 (section 31 rule (12)) and citing it in both claims rather than by deleting the claims.
CL-M112-Q02-005 and CL-M112-Q02-010 rest wholly on PROV-M112-009, a provision the map itself marks as not applicable to the matter date. Marked disputed.
temporal_issues: PROV-M112-009 (Notaries Ordinance s.34) is the 31-2022 s.17 substitution; the corpus holds neither the pre-2022 section nor the Schedules to the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005, so the April 2018 offence and penalty cannot be stated. Correctly excluded from the indispensable set, but two Q02 claims still rest on it.

PROV-M112-010 (section 31 rule (6)): the researcher's temporal note is wrong that the rule was never substituted - 31-2022 s.16(4) substituted it, re-enacting the identical words. Note corrected; provision downgraded to partially_verified.

PROV-M112-005 (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2): the operative words and paragraph (a) in the corpus are the 30-2022 and 4-2024 text. 30-2022 s.2 shows the pre-2022 section ended with words beginning "shall be of force", but that wording is not in the corpus. Provision downgraded to partially_verified and CL-M112-Q01-001 marked disputed.

Not an error, but recorded: the corpus amendment log for section 31 attaches "repeal by 31-2022 s.16(12)" to the rule (26) span, whereas 31-2022 s.16(12) reads "by the repeal of rule (27) thereof". The researcher noticed the oddity and set it aside; it is a corpus mapping fault, and rule (26) stood in April 2018 and still stands.

Also recorded: in April 2018 the list accompanying both the rule (26)(a)(i) return and the rule (29) certified copy was in the Form F; the Form F 1 in the consolidation comes from 6-2024 s.3(8) and (9). Both excerpts stop short of the form reference, so no claim is affected.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Section 31 rule (12), the execution-in-the-notary's-presence rule, was missing and has been added as PROV-M112-901.

Section 32(1) exempts rule (16) as to boundaries and rule (26) for five classes of instrument, none of which covers an ordinary transfer of Sri Lankan land, so no exception applies here. Not added, because it changes nothing on these facts.

Section 4(2) and section 3(1) of the Notaries Ordinance each confer practice "within the judicial zone in which he resides" and are an alternative route to the same result as section 4A. Not added, because section 4A already carries the point and adding them would inflate the hop count.
Section 31 rule (8) (at least two witnesses subscribing) underlies the two-witness fact in the enriched backgrounds but is not cited. Left alone: the questions do not turn on it.

The Notaries Ordinance definition section (s.43) defines only "Council of Legal Education", "High Court Judge" and "Registrar-General". Neither "area", "judicial zone" nor "district" is defined in the corpus, so the reach of the Colombo warrant rests on section 4A alone.
case_law_dependence: None. No answer part cites a case, and none needs one: the area rule, the disqualification rule and the out-of-district transmission duty are all stated in terms in section 31.
enrichment_issues: FACT-M112-Q04-002 ("both Councils were duly constituted and functioning ... and neither stood dissolved") exists only to switch off the proviso to 12-2006 s.9 and so hints at the existence of that proviso. It names no statute and states no conclusion, so it is left as it stands, but it is the closest any added fact comes to a leak.
No enriched background names a statute, a section or a rule, and none states or implies the answer. Checked all four.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: The four enriched backgrounds repeat the same land description, execution date and office address. That is consistent rather than duplicative, since each question is answered on its own background, but a lawyer should confirm the repetition is intended.

The Q01 added-fact text FACT-M112-Q01-003 says "the vendor, Waruna Liyanage and two witnesses" while the enriched background names "Nimal Wickramasinghe, Waruna Liyanage and two witnesses". Same facts, different wording; harmless.

lawyer_questions: Q04: does the property-situated limb of s.9 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act govern a deed of transfer, so that duty on this Matara land is payable to the Southern Provincial Council even though the deed is executed in Colombo? If so the question is answerable and only the receiving office or prescribed bank remains missing from the corpus.

Q02: was a breach of rule (29) an offence under s.34 of the Notaries Ordinance in April 2018, and what was the fine then? The corpus holds only the 2022 substitution and not the Schedules to the Increase of Fines Act No. 12 of 2005.
Q01: did rule (6) of s.31 read in April 2018 exactly as Act No. 31 of 2022 s.16(4) re-enacted it?
Q01: did s.2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, in its pre-2022 form, require attestation by a licensed notary before two or more witnesses in the terms CL-M112-Q01-001 states?
Q03: is there a rate order or regulation fixing stamp duty on a transfer of immovable property in the Southern Province as at March 2018 that should be added to the corpus?
